sentences.title: The First Stone
sentences.text: On a foggy night in Low Marrow, the river ran black beneath the trees.

sentences.text: A villager stepped from the muddy bank into the wooden ferryboat, shivering as his boots hit the floorboards.

sentences.text: He carried no coin purse, only a heavy posture and eyes wet with regret.

sentences.title: The First Stone
sentences.text: His shoulders dropped, the bitter anger vanished from his face, and he stared toward the market shore, unable to recall why he had wept.

sentences.title: The First Stone
sentences.text: "Step across," the Ferryman said quietly.

tags.quote: "Step across," the Ferryman said quietly.

sentences.title: The First Stone
sentences.text: Once, in Low Marrow, the ferry cost one memory.

sentences.text: Three dawns later, morning mist hung thick over the river.

sentences.text: The Fisherman boarded the ferry, a heavy coil of rope slung over his shoulder and a dark wool cap pulled low.

sentences.title: Unburdening the Fisherman
sentences.text: He twisted the frayed fibers of the rope in his hands, trembling as he stared into the swirling currents.

sentences.title: Unburdening the Fisherman
sentences.text: Months had passed since the spring flood, yet every time he closed his eyes, he heard the timber beams of his cottage snapping against the wall of water.

tags.quote: every time he closed his eyes, he heard the timber beams of his cottage snapping against the wall of water.

sentences.text: He could still see his nets tearing in the mud, his livestock drowning in the dark.

sentences.text: The Ferryman lifted his hand, holding his broad palm steady beneath the rising sun.

sentences.text: The Fisherman leaned down and breathed the terror of that night into the old man's grip—the roaring water, the screaming wind, the loss of everything he owned.

sentences.text: The Ferryman closed his fingers tight.

sentences.title: Unburdening the Fisherman
sentences.text: When he opened them, a second smooth pale stone rested in his hand.

sentences.text: He placed it beside the first on the timber floorboards of the hull.

sentences.title: Unburdening the Fisherman
sentences.text: The Fisherman exhaled deeply.

sentences.title: Unburdening the Fisherman
sentences.text: He smoothed his cap, slung his rope higher, and looked out across the quiet grey water.

sentences.title: Unburdening the Fisherman
sentences.text: The memory was gone.

sentences.title: Unburdening the Fisherman
sentences.text: He no longer remembered why he had ever feared the river's mudbank, or why he had wept upon the shore.

sentences.title: Unburdening the Fisherman
sentences.text: He smiled, unburdened and light.

sentences.title: The Mayor's Weekly Fare
sentences.text: Word of the painless ferry spread through the cottages of Low Marrow.

sentences.title: The Mayor's Weekly Fare
sentences.text: Before long, villagers arrived at the riverbank every day to trade away their shame, debts, and broken promises.

sentences.title: The Mayor's Weekly Fare
sentences.text: The Mayor crossed most often of all.

sentences.title: The Mayor's Weekly Fare
sentences.text: Stout and ruddy-faced, he wore a bright crimson sash and a heavy brass chain of office.

tags.quote: Stout and ruddy-faced, he wore a bright crimson sash and a heavy brass chain of office.

sentences.title: The Mayor's Weekly Fare
sentences.text: He stepped onto the ferry boat every week, flushed with temper from fierce town council disputes or public embarrassments.

sentences.title: The Mayor's Weekly Fare
sentences.text: He reached habitually for his coin purse before remembering the fare.

sentences.title: The Mayor's Weekly Fare
sentences.text: Leaning over the Ferryman's open palm, the Mayor whispered away the memory of his bad decisions and sharp words.

sentences.title: The Mayor's Weekly Fare
sentences.text: The Ferryman closed his hand, produced another pale river stone, and set it carefully alongside the others.

sentences.title: The Mayor's Weekly Fare
sentences.text: Immediately, the Mayor’s scowl vanished.

sentences.title: The Mayor's Weekly Fare
sentences.text: He adjusted his brass chain, crossed his arms proudly over his sash, and laughed with unearned confidence as the boat drifted toward the market shore.

sentences.title: The Mayor's Weekly Fare
sentences.text: The villagers grew light and kind, greeting each other with cheerful smiles in the muddy streets.

sentences.text: But with each crossing, the Ferryman’s boat sat lower in the water.

sentences.title: Rebuilding on the Mudbank
sentences.text: Two months passed, bringing clear dawn light over the low banks of Low Marrow.

sentences.title: Rebuilding on the Mudbank
sentences.text: From the middle of the river, the Ferryman rested his heavy oars and watched the shore.

sentences.title: Rebuilding on the Mudbank
sentences.text: On the flat mudbank right at the water’s edge, the young Fisherman was hard at work.

sentences.title: Rebuilding on the Mudbank
sentences.text: He whistled a bright tune, driving thick timber posts into the dark silt with heavy iron blows.

sentences.title: Rebuilding on the Mudbank
sentences.text: Slung over his shoulder was the same coil of frayed rope he always carried, but his face held no shadow of past terror.

sentences.title: Rebuilding on the Mudbank
sentences.text: The Ferryman recognized the exact patch of ground.

sentences.title: Rebuilding on the Mudbank
sentences.text: Only two springs ago, the rising river had torn through this low bank, splintering the Fisherman’s cottage and sweeping his possessions downstream.

sentences.title: Rebuilding on the Mudbank
sentences.text: The Fisherman had stood on the shore then, weeping for everything he had lost.

sentences.title: Rebuilding on the Mudbank
sentences.text: Now, unburdened by the memory of that terrible thaw, the young man hammered his new foundations into the soft silt.

sentences.title: Rebuilding on the Mudbank
sentences.text: He smiled at the cool water lapping against his boots, unaware that he was building his home directly in the path of the next flood.

tags.quote: unaware that he was building his home directly in the path of the next flood.

sentences.title: Rebuilding on the Mudbank
sentences.text: Without the weight of past disaster to guide his hands, he walked joyfully back into the very danger that had once destroyed him.

sentences.title: The New Bridge Plan
sentences.text: By noon the following day, the Mayor stood on the muddy bank beside two ancient, moss-covered stone piers.

sentences.title: The New Bridge Plan
sentences.text: Dark water swirled around the ruined masonry, all that remained of the old bridge that had collapsed long ago.

tags.quote: Dark water swirled around the ruined masonry, all that remained of the old bridge that had collapsed long ago.

sentences.title: The New Bridge Plan
sentences.text: Adjusting his heavy brass chain over his crimson sash, the Mayor gestured grandly toward the opposite shore.

sentences.title: The New Bridge Plan
sentences.text: He announced a plan to construct a magnificent new stone bridge directly upon those broken piers, reconnecting the trade routes once and for all.

tags.quote: He announced a plan to construct a magnificent new stone bridge directly upon those broken piers, reconnecting the trade routes once and for all.

sentences.title: The New Bridge Plan
sentences.text: The Ferryman pulled his wooden boat to the landing and stepped onto the mud.

sentences.title: The New Bridge Plan
sentences.text: He looked at the cracked stone, then spoke directly to the civic leader.

sentences.title: The New Bridge Plan
sentences.text: "The riverbed beneath those piers is soft sand," the Ferryman said.

tags.quote: "The riverbed beneath those piers is soft sand," the Ferryman said.

sentences.title: The New Bridge Plan
sentences.text: "When the spring tides rise, the current undercuts the foundation.

sentences.title: The New Bridge Plan
sentences.text: That is why the old bridge cracked and fell."

sentences.title: The New Bridge Plan
sentences.text: The Mayor’s cheerful expression faltered.

sentences.title: The New Bridge Plan
sentences.text: A sudden wave of irritation and sharp anxiety tightened his chest.

sentences.title: The New Bridge Plan
sentences.text: The Ferryman’s words stirred an uncomfortable doubt he did not wish to bear.

sentences.title: The New Bridge Plan
sentences.text: The Mayor stared at the piers, his pride wounded by the sudden threat of failure.

sentences.title: The New Bridge Plan
sentences.text: Refusing to let caution derail his grand project, the Mayor turned away from the river and eyed the Ferryman's waiting boat.

tags.quote: Refusing to let caution derail his grand project, the Mayor turned away from the river and eyed the Ferryman's waiting boat.

sentences.title: Trading the Warning
sentences.text: Late that afternoon, as the sun dipped behind the timber cottages, the Mayor stepped onto the wooden ferry.

sentences.title: Trading the Warning
sentences.text: He could not endure the lingering worry that the new bridge might collapse.

tags.quote: He could not endure the lingering worry that the new bridge might collapse.

sentences.title: Trading the Warning
sentences.text: Leaning close to the Ferryman’s stooped shoulder, the Mayor cupped his hands and whispered the warning he had just received into the Ferryman’s open palm.

sentences.title: Trading the Warning
sentences.text: He handed over the memory of the soft riverbed, the crumbling sand, and the Ferryman’s grave words.

sentences.title: Trading the Warning
sentences.text: The Ferryman closed his dark fingers around the spoken secret.

sentences.title: Trading the Warning
sentences.text: When he opened his hand, a smooth pale stone rested in his palm.

sentences.title: Trading the Warning

sentences.title: Trading the Warning
sentences.text: With a deep breath, the Mayor stood tall.

sentences.title: Trading the Warning
sentences.text: The anxious crease on his brow vanished entirely.

sentences.title: Trading the Warning
sentences.text: He adjusted his brass chain, smiled at the distant shoreline, and forgot that anyone had ever spoken of danger.

sentences.title: Trading the Warning
sentences.text: The Ferryman watched the Mayor step onto the far bank with unburdened confidence.

sentences.title: Trading the Warning
sentences.text: But inside the hull, the new stone pressed down with sudden weight.

sentences.title: Trading the Warning
sentences.text: The wooden boat settled deeper into the river, its upper rim floating mere inches above the dark, silent water.

sentences.title: The Keeper of Reasons
sentences.text: Dusk settled over the grey river as workers laid the final arch of the new stone bridge directly upon the ancient, cracked piers.

sentences.title: The Keeper of Reasons
sentences.text: Standing at the water’s edge, the Ferryman looked up at the structure, then turned to the Mayor.

sentences.title: The Keeper of Reasons
sentences.text: For the first time, the Ferryman broke his silence.

sentences.title: The Keeper of Reasons
sentences.text: He described how sixty winters ago, heavy rains had scoured the sandy riverbed, causing those exact piers to tilt and crumble beneath the masonry.

tags.quote: how sixty winters ago, heavy rains had scoured the sandy riverbed, causing those exact piers to tilt and crumble beneath the masonry.

sentences.title: The Keeper of Reasons
sentences.text: He spoke of the families who had wept, the ruined trade, and the hard lessons the village had once pledged never to abandon.

sentences.title: The Keeper of Reasons
sentences.text: He explained that in surrendering their grief to his boat, they had not merely discarded their pain; they had given away every reason they possessed for caution.

tags.quote: they had given away every reason they possessed for caution.

sentences.title: The Keeper of Reasons
sentences.text: The Mayor listened politely, a soft smile resting on his face.

sentences.title: The Keeper of Reasons
sentences.text: He smoothed down his crimson sash, then held out an open palm over the ferry’s rim.

sentences.title: The Keeper of Reasons
sentences.text: "And what would it cost to forget this too?"

sentences.title: The Keeper of Reasons
sentences.text: He realized the quiet terror of his trade: any truth he offered would only be returned to him as another fare.
